name: Another Tomorrow
band_note: mean of blouse and sweater entry $420 (women's price pass, 2026-10-13)
why: Women's tailoring, coats, knitwear, trousers and denim in traceable natural fibres, jackets around $1,300, sold through its own site, SoHo flagship and Nordstrom.
origin: Founded in 2018 by Vanessa Barboni Hallik.

ownership.owner: Another Tomorrow Inc. (founder-led; shareholders not published)

quote.q: My mission is to create a truly sustainable and compassionate company with a three-pronged approach of providing a foundational wardrobe of ethically and responsibly made clothing…
quote.who: Vanessa Barboni Hallik, founder and CEO
quote.src: A Note From Our Founder, anothertomorrow.co

opview: “My mission is to create a truly sustainable and compassionate company with a three-pronged approach of providing a foundational wardrobe of ethically and responsibly made clothing…” — Vanessa Barboni Hallik, founder and CEO, A Note From Our Founder, anothertomorrow.co

facts_read.source: brand site; B Lab directory; Nordstrom search; Vinted catalogue page; TRR designer directory; B Lab directory; GOTS database

fibre.sample: stratified sample of 80 across 8 product-type groups, proportional; 195 styles from 366 new clothing listings in /products.json (492 total; Authenticated Resale

tech_evidence.names: licensed fibres: Tencel lyocell blends (core jersey), Seacell lyocell, Naia Renew acetate; house 'seasonless, farm-traceable' merino
tech_evidence.owned: licensed fibres; digital product passport per garment via EVRYTHNG (traceability, not fabric)
tech_evidence.share: 10% of sample (8 of 80) in a licensed named fibre

craft_evidence.owned: no — cut-and-sew suppliers in Italy and Portugal, visited but deliberately not named
craft_evidence.makers: no (garment towns named per product: Messina, Bergamo, Correzzola, Torre Pallavicina, Braga and others)
craft_evidence.mills: yes — Candiani (denim mill); wool farms Lake Hawea Station (NZ), Py-Aguazú and La Cuchilla (Uruguay); Tier-2 mills listed on the Open Apparel Registry
craft_evidence.madein: 69% (55 of 80: Italy 52, Portugal 3); most of the rest name the fabric's knitting or weaving town instead
craft_evidence.heritage: none dated — values-led founder story; Soho flagship
craft_evidence.process: yes — supplier pages for the denim mill and wool farms, a where-we-produce policy (living wages checked against two benchmarks, every factory visited), and a QR provenance journey per garment
craft_evidence.reasoning: Mills and farms are named and documented (Candiani, Lake Hawea Station, two Uruguayan farms), and product pages place the garment in a named Italian or Portuguese town. The cut-and-sew makers are withheld by policy, so the maker is not verifiable from the store: a strong 3.

notes.tech: Thread proposed 2 (2026-10-14): named fabrics licensed fibres: Tencel lyocell blends (core jersey), Seacell lyocell, Naia Renew acetate; house 'seasonless, farm-traceable' merino, 10% of sample (8 of 80) in a licensed named fibre of the range. Seated as proposed, pending ruling.
